questions.q: What name is given to the high land that separates one drainage basin from another?
questions.why: The watershed is the ridge of high land that divides drainage basins.

questions.q: Which process is when rocks carried by a river knock against each other and become smaller and rounder?
questions.why: Attrition is rock against rock; abrasion is rock against the bed and banks.

questions.q: On a meander, what forms on the inside of the bend?
questions.why: Water is slow and shallow on the inside, so material is deposited, forming a slip-off slope.

questions.model: A river flows over hard rock lying above softer rock. The soft rock is eroded faster by hydraulic action and abrasion, undercutting the hard rock and creating a plunge pool. The overhang collapses and the waterfall retreats upstream, leaving a gorge.
points: hard rock over soft rock; soft rock eroded faster / undercutting
waterfall retreats upstream leaving a gorge
